headline: Chemistry World reports that a Microsoft AI system for planning how to make chemical compounds, described as having a split personality, is a fast learner.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: only the headline is available, so what the system does and how well it works are unverified.
importance_line: Chemists and drug-discovery teams who plan how to make new molecules would be affected first, then the companies that sell such tools, but what the system does, how quickly it learns and how it was tested are unknown.
summary: Chemistry World reports that Microsoft has developed a retrosynthesis AI, software that works backwards from a target molecule to suggest how to build it from simpler ingredients, which it describes as having a split personality and being a fast learner.
notes: Chemistry World returned a Human Verification page (HTTP 405) and no other outlet carrying the story was found, so the entry rests on the headline. What 'split personality' means is not known, so the entry only repeats the phrase.
